calls.head: This one’s going to leave marks
calls.body: The Mammoth and the Rangers are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 116.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Utah 110 (5th), NY Rangers 121 (2nd)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 120, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

calls.head: The Mammoth will outshoot the Rangers
calls.body: The Mammoth are one of the league’s best for shot volume, at the relentless end; the Rangers are near the bottom of the league, at the selective end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Mammoth take more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Rangers.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Utah had 69.5 per 60 and NY Rangers 49.0 per 60. Coming in, Utah was at 64.5 per 60 and NY Rangers at 52.4 per 60.

NYR.head: We had this close to even (56% for NY Rangers), and NY Rangers came through.

UTA.head: We had this close to even (44% for Utah), and it went NY Rangers’s way.

surprises.head: NY Rangers got the good looks
surprises.body: NY Rangers’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 125 games.

surprises.head: NY Rangers shortened their bench
surprises.body: NY Rangers’s bottom-six forwards played 35% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: The Rangers beat the Mammoth
paras: Vladislav Gavrikov opened the scoring late in the first. Four different Rangers scored. J.T. Miller scored the winner midway through the third.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Rangers.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
